target.title: fix(commands): distinguish user No from Cancel in confirm prompts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user answers No to Proceed with reset? or Proceed with uninstall? in `src/commands/reset.ts:119` and `src/commands/uninstall.ts:173`, the condition `isCancel(ok) || !ok` treats it identically to Ctrl+C cancel, showing Reset cancelled. / Uninstall cancelled. This is misleading the user didnt cancel they explicitly declined.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bug is in the condition itself: isCancel checks for Ctrl+C/Escape (the @clack/prompts cancel symbol), while !ok catches the user clicking No. These are semantically distinct user intents and should produce different messages.

## User Impact

- Before: Answering No shows Reset cancelled. despite not being a cancellation
- After: No shows Reset skipped.; only Ctrl+C/Escape shows cancelled
- Functionally identical: both paths exit(0)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** User No conflated with Cancel in confirm prompts
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24, commit `5ea73a1e6` on branch `fix/confirm-no-vs-cancel` (rebased on upstream/main `94e1cc9a4`)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts` with a test that mocks `@clack/prompts.confirm` to return `false` (No) and `Symbol.for("clack:cancel")` (Ctrl+C), then calls the real `resetCommand()` with a mock runtime and verifies the output messages and exit codes
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node`/`vitest` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  stdout | src/commands/verify-reset-vitest.test.ts > shows skipped (not cancelled) when user answers No
  Test 1 (No): log=["Reset skipped."]
  Test 1 (No): exit=[0]

  stdout | src/commands/verify-reset-vitest.test.ts > shows cancelled when user presses Ctrl+C
  [CANCEL]: Reset cancelled.
  Test 2 (Cancel): log=[]
  Test 2 (Cancel): exit=[0]

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  2 passed (2)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real `resetCommand` invocation: when user answers No, output is "Reset skipped." (not "cancelled"); when user presses Ctrl+C, output is "Reset cancelled." via cancel(). Both paths exit(0) correctly.
- **What was not tested:** `uninstallCommand` (same fix pattern applies symmetrically); live CLI prompt interaction

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test src/commands/reset.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       3 passed (3)
```

Existing command tests pass. Real `resetCommand` invocation verified via vitest with mocked @clack/prompts.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes message changes from cancelled to skipped when user answers No
- Config/env/migration behavior: No
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No
- Highest-risk area: Message string change
- Mitigation: Both paths exit(0) identically; only the display message changes; real `resetCommand` invocation verifies behavior

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
